The measured before/after is a count: non-test producers of a RoleScheduler Caller 0 -> 1, and reachability of domain.ActorTypeLoop for Requirement.RequestedBy through a transport false -> true. ROW 3 -- what it records but does not fix: (a) the openapi document declares at contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml lines 5-8 that increment decomposition/planning 'remains a loop scheduler responsibility' while internal/application/service.go's Plan (:888) and Prepare (:1023) accept RoleOwner and 23 test files call one of the two, so the declaration and the application-layer role pair disagree; that is a statement about the public HTTP surface, where neither command has a route at all, and it is recorded here for the tech_lead rather than resolved. The figure is recorded WITH ITS PATTERN so it can never be ambiguous again: `grep -c '^--- SKIP'` counts TOP-LEVEL skips and gives 26, and `grep -cE '^ *--- SKIP'` counts skipped subtests too and gives 49. Both were measured on the same captured output in this worktree, so the coordinator's 49 and this task's 26 are one fact under two patterns and neither figure is wrong. Either way that package's run measured nothing about this change; it is recorded under gate rule G7 and never counted as a pass. (e) NOTHING remains on A6: it was first reported as UNMET and is now MET, and the history is kept rather than tidied away. The implementer escalated A6's three conditions as irreconcilable; the tech_lead ruled that they reconcile if the predicate does not live in cmd/control-plane, and the ruling is right. The predicate is now internal/api.NewCombinedAuthenticator plus CombinedAuthenticator.IdentityConfigurationError, run() calls the constructor and returns its error, and the start-time refusal is proven by EXECUTING the binary; the request-boundary refusal is kept as defence in depth. See the api record's a6-* checks. The superseded reasoning was: A6 asks both that the process 'fail to start' when RECONCILE_IDENTITY is also in OWNER_EMAILS and that nothing else in cmd/control-plane/main.go change and that the refusal be asserted through the authenticator; the two halves conflict, so the refusal is implemented and tested in CombinedAuthenticator.Authenticate (every IAP-authenticated request is refused with a message naming the conflict) and NO start-time guard was added -- recorded as a partial, escalated to the tech_lead, not reinterpreted -- and the escalation is what produced the ruling that fixed it. checks.name: a14-determinism-in-the-new-runner-tests
checks.summary: A14 MEASURED over every new and modified test. No new or modified test contains time.Sleep, time.After, time.NewTimer, time.Tick, time.Now, `go ` (a goroutine), math/rand or crypto/rand: verified by grepping the four touched test files for each of those tokens. Every clock is injected: internal/api's new fixture uses framingClock, the steppable injected clock the V2-082 chain test already introduced, advanced only by its own nextDay() method; internal/runner's new tests reuse the package's existing journeyClock, which returns a fixed time.Unix(1700000000, 0).UTC(); internal/application's new tests use the package's existing service() helper and its fixed clock. The whole suite was run with -race and -count=1 and reported ok for every package. QUOTA: the in-memory adapter does not true up its quota reservation, so quota.ReadTransactionUsage (Reads 6001, Writes 1, at internal/quota/quota.go:56) admits only FOUR read transactions per budget day against quota.DefaultBudget's 25000 reads (internal/quota/quota.go:46).
